neutral_rate_rekeyed.note: a readout, not the default: r* with its capex term on the other key; the macro path, and so the required return, is unchanged; the demand layer (the central variant) is run on each r*. On the central (the refit, keyed to replacement investment / income, alpha_inv = macro.NEUTRAL_SCALE) the term is replaced by alpha_capex 0.25 x the pace of tasks moving (the key as tuned on (b)). On the comparator (b) (keyed to the pace) by alpha_inv x the change in investment / income at two scales: the bridge's (alpha_capex converted at (b)'s start) and the demand layer's ((1 - a1)/a_r of the IS curve). The series keyed to is replacement investment, the only investment in the quasi-static accounts; net investment (Vm dK/dt / income) is a diagnostic only: the machine stock falls on every deep path, (b) included, so keying to it would lower r* further.
